content: # Two computers and a cable: running coding LLMs off the cloud

hi all, today i will reveal to you the details of my home ai laboratory development setup composed of two gaming computers stacked one on top of another, with ethernet, stupid amount of intel x64 cores, and many other twists. i've been working on building this stack a really long time now, and its starting to approach completion - so I thought it was time to share!
## Why bother

cloud coding assistants are pay per use. you get your monthly allowance, but what if you burn through it mid-project, and then its either wait or pay scalper fees. a local model doesn't meter anything. except your wall. it runs on hardware you manage manually, it won't randomly vanish one day, and on my own network no data ever leaves the house.

i warn you that its much slower and dumber than models they offer on the internet :) yet the process of setting up this configuration, as well as being able to access it completely on demand completely outweighs any negatives
## The layout
│  MINIFRIDGE (dev)            │
│  RX 6800 16GB · 64GB RAM     │
│  VS Code + Copilot (BYOK)    │
│ direct Ethernet
│  WS-RARETOWER (inference)    │
│  Ollama - GLM-4.7-Flash      │

**WS-RARETOWER** is the inference box. it holds the model in video memory and answers requests. the only number that matters here is 24GB of VRAM - that decides which models fit and which ones don't. everything else in the machine can be assumed to be completely undefined.
here be dragons - always account for minimum functional specification.

**MINIFRIDGE** is where i actually sit and work. editor, containers, projects, almost entirely through VS Code. included GPU which optionally hosts a smaller fallback model, avoids hot-swapping models on the main box in the middle of a task.
they are networked through an ethernet switch. any capacity should be fine (they trade HTTP traffic)
## The software
**Ollama** (free) runs the model. you install it, you pull a model, and it exposes a completely static HTTP api.
**GLM-4.7-Flash** is a model I've been testing - 31 billion parameters, open weights, about 3 billion fire per token.
the trick to getting a model to fit on a consumer card and still feel responsive is finding the right size.
**VS Code + GitHub Copilot** on the dev machine act as mainframe: pointed at the ollama endpoint through the bring-your-own-key option they serve: chat, agent mode, inline ghost-text completions.
> more to follow!

content.heading: thirteenth post (#mixing, #phase, #technique, #audio, #music)
content: i found a mixing technique by accident and now i can't stop using it
* i usually build my final mixes from 3 "core" channels
* 1 is not enough
> one gets fully inverted
> one gets max-stereo-widened
> one gets narrowed
* sometimes the narrowed one is also inverted
* i never really planned that
* it just felt correct
* i clone that narrowed-inverted one again
* run it through a limiter
* feed it back in
* odd number of total inversions, always
> 3 minimum, sometimes 5
* even number ruins it
* this clone-feed is what causes the phase-artifact-cancellation
* not the widening
* i was wrong about that part for a while
* the weird part: it only fully reveals itself at the very end of a track
* my fades are never uniform
> one channel has tape-grain decay
> one has a slope to zero
> one just stops dead after the reverbeve  tail
* while the track is at full volume, the cancellation holds
* everything sums clean
* once the three channels start fading at different rates, the limiter on the cloned channel can't keep up
* its release-time stops matching the actual decay-curve
* so the cancellation breaks
> just slightly
> just at the edges of the stereo field
* what's left over sounds like a alias
> a little ghost-image of the track, right as it dies out
> i didn't design this on purpose
> i reverse-engineered it after noticing it on my last upload
> now that i understand it, i think i can tune it
> push the alias earlier or later in the fade
> make it louder or more narrow
> just by adjusting the limiter's release-time against my fade-curves
* a sort-of fade-localized-deliberate-aliasing-tool, i guess
* **if you want to try this**: 3 channels, odd inversions:
> clone+limit the narrowed one
> feed it back into the sum
> give your channels mismatched fade shapes
> listen to what survives at the very end

content.heading: curiosity
content.content: i wanted to discuss my findings in qwen3.5, specifically how I managed to get it to produce useful output and terminate in one session, after 1 chat message, followed by an interrupt, followed by another request

content.heading: ramble
content: the model refused to terminate aggressively, running on consumer hardware, on a baseline ollama instance.
a simple query of 'what are your patchnotes' resulted in a non-terminating process where the model was attempting to look up knowledge, but was getting distracted with the formatting of the output.
the model refused to interpret the statement relating to its output shape as a hint, rather using it as an excuse to keep producing more output.

interrupting the model, and adding a guidance interpreted from its partial output managed to produce a extremely lengthy response, but one that finished with the clause of formatting being slightly misinterpreted.
what i found interesting was the fact that the model did manage to not only give an innacurate answer,
it also managed to think itself into contradicting itself

it carried on making the assumption that its knowledge was correct and current at any given timeframe immutable and reasoned from there to conclude that the formatting directive provided to it, was to be doubted as malicious information.

the guidance it was given to simplify the response to one statement was skipped, somehow the request to format the ouput as 5 plain text lines proved troublesome to the model, despite supposedly being adept at transforming basic text, as well as structured data.
the implied freedom to respond without forced text formatting was sidestepped.
the model chose to format the text specifically into 5 lines, be that when giving a valid response, or notifying of an error
no concrete contract was made with the model, perhaps causing more trouble than not
